scope: Matched held-out MiniMax-H3 NF4 baseline versus native Ref2VA identity-LoRA smoke ablation
summary: The first six-step rank-8 identity LoRA was reproducibly trained and evaluated, but it was rejected because the conservative identity floor fell by 0.0302 and motion adherence fell by 0.0996.
evidence: Training completed 6/6 optimizer steps and produced a 32,825,120-byte checkpoint with SHA-256 a7a92f68339e271562742a7b93054e489801d569dffb1cb663f22453358a2731.
Matched held-out generation kept the same MiniMax-H3 NF4 backbone, reference, scene anchor, seed, dimensions, frame count, and inference steps; only the LoRA differed.
DINOv2 identity floor changed from 0.8808738291 to 0.8507119119, an identity gain of -0.0301619172.
Motion adherence changed from 1.0 to 0.9004063777; scene preservation and temporal consistency passed their non-regression gates.
No full-frame semantic topology review was available, so the strict topology gate failed closed.
lessons: A short identity-only smoke curriculum can weaken both worst-frame identity and action adherence even when mean visual quality looks plausible.
Similarity proxies cannot substitute for full-frame head, torso, shoulder, arm-chain, and limb-count review.
RSI promotion must remain bounded and gate every candidate against the unchanged backbone.
limitations: This result uses third-party NF4 MiniMax-H3 weights rather than the official BF16 checkpoint.
The ablation contains one held-out 39-frame synthetic/control demo and does not establish general model quality.
The rejected candidate is not suitable for release.
next_actions: Evaluate the topology-targeted dataset round on the 124-frame held-out inspect-flower sequence.
Promote only if full-frame semantic topology and motion, scene, and temporal non-regression gates pass.
